dedupe_keys.name: pyronear open source camera based early wildfire detection system with models edge engine and open image data

description: Pyronear is a French non-profit association that co-develops, with volunteers and partners, an open-source system for early detection of wildfire starts in natural areas from cameras, designed to be automatic, low-energy, inexpensive and modular so that fire and rescue services can respond quickly. Its code is fully open, and it builds an annotated image dataset that it shares as open data. Coverage: developed in France; where cameras are deployed was not read. The pyro-vision library provides wildfire image classification models in PyTorch with pretrained weights; the pyro-engine repository contains the detection engine that runs models on edge devices connected to an alert API, and a camera control API with adapters for several camera types, plus deployment and calibration scripts. Format and access: Python code on GitHub; the site is in French; free. Licence: Apache 2.0 for pyro-vision and pyro-engine, read from their licence files; the licence of the image dataset was not read. Caveats: the dataset's location, size and licence were not read, and the deployed networks and their performance were not checked. Simulation uses: detection timing assumptions and camera network design for wildfire emergency response around infrastructure corridors and settlements. Related records: WRF-SFIRE (model-openwfm-wrf-sfire-coupled-weather-fire) simulates fire spread, and BC Wildfire Predictive Services (platform-bcgov-wildfire-predictive-services) supports operational decisions.
